links.reason: 1395 (முரிந்தன... குருதி நீத்தமே) only narrates carnage and states no claim about victory, so it cannot conflict with the poem's அமர்மிகல் யாவது?; a difference of genre and tone is not a tension, and the epic gains no question from a verse that does not ask it.

2868 (உயிர்க் கொலையும் வேண்டா) says killing brings suffering; Tirumanthiram 200 lists கொலையே களவுகள் காமம் பொய் and gives up of them as the way to Siva's feet. Neither verse states how release comes, so the claimed karma-versus-grace opposition is imported; they share a prohibition.

81 (இளமையின் இயல்பிது... கிளைமையும் அனையதே) is the king's own reflection on youth and kin; T2100 is an obscure verse (the marker flags it) whose last lines say the days before grey hair are few. They agree on urgency; 'develops' and the Saiva 'statement of the same urgency' rest on an uncertain reading of the Tirumanthiram.

406 (பிற அறம் அல்ல பேசார்... துறவறம் புணர்க) does set renunciation over other dharma, against Kural 46's அறத்தாற்றின் இல்வாழ்க்கை... புறத்தாற்றில் போஒய்ப் பெறுவ தெவன். But the verse's speaker is uncertain, and the gains clause about an ascetic who lived in a merchant's house is not in either text; it reads closer to a tension than a qualification.
links.text_issue: Speaker of lines 1-3 and referent of line 4 not fixed by the verse.

links.reason: 25 lists the boar shot and the enemy's killing in one summary line (பன்றி எய்து... பகை நாம் அறக் கொன்ற); 2204 shows the shot, so a prologue-to-scene link is real, but 'the opening blow of the war' is not stated in either verse. This is summary and event, which the graph already tracks.
links.text_issue: Both verses flagged uncertain; 25 line 4 subject unclear.

links.reason: 1545 line 4 (பெற்றார் மகப்பெற்றார்... பிறர்மக்கள் பிறரே) withholds மக்கள் from bodily children, while Kural 63 only reports that people call மக்கள் தம்பொருள். The clash depends on reading தம்தம் வினை one way; the note hedges on this, so it is a defensible contrast, not an incompatible claim.

Soolamani and Purananuru share the contrast தனக்கென வாழாப் பிறர்க்கு உரியாளன் / தமக்கென முயலா... பிறர்க்கென முயலுநர், but in different words, not four-word runs. The inference that the maxim 'was already a phrase of praise' dates the usage with nothing in the texts to show it.

69 (ஒற்றைவெண் குடையின் ஈழல் உலகு கண்படுப்ப) has no claim about the fall; the note's warning is supplied by the reader from NT 3's குடைநிழற்கீழ்... வீழ்வர். The shared umbrella is an image, not a qualification, and the verse does not stop short of anything.

244 gives fruits for the vows (ஒளியினோடு அழகு வென்றி) and flesh-abstention (புலைசு தேன்கள் ஒருவிய பயனும்); Kural 255 gives the fear of hell. Both gains clauses are true, but lines 1-2 do not say which vow yields which fruit, and 'qualifies' fits less well than 'adds a second reason'.

2101 (புலம்பு கொண்டனர்) records the sons' wailing and does not say it comes from attachment, so the verse illustrates Kural 347 (பற்றினைப் பற்றி விடாதவர்க்கு இடும்பைகள்) by the reader's inference. 'Qualifies' names no condition or limit.

2088 (சிறியவர் செய்த தீமை... பெரியவர் பொறுப்பர்) shows him yielding and ending the sulk (ஊடல் நீக்கினான்); the vow that makes his defeat the winning of her is in another verse, not in the unit. It illustrates Kural 1327; it does not show that he wins by losing.

465 (செய்தவ முடையளென்பார்) is the crowd's guess and 1912 (தவத்தது விளைவிலாதேன்) is the mother's feeling at the reunion; the two do not conflict, since the reunion shows the penance did bear fruit. 'Tension' overstates it; the earlier-claim-answered pattern fits qualifies.
links.text_issue: 1912 lines 3-4 (தாளையா... றோளையா) are hard to divide; the sense is a reading.

links.reason: Manimekalai line 90 (மக்கள் யாக்கை உணவின் பிண்டம்) and Purananuru 18 line 20 (உண்டி முதற்றே உணவின் பிண்டம்) share the words உணவின் பிண்டம், and both draw a conclusion about hunger from them. The Sangam poet makes it the king's duty to feed by water; the goddess makes it the reason for a mantra (இரும் பசி அறுக்கும்). The pairing shows one maxim put to two uses.

564 (உலக நூலும் குலங்களும் முறையும்... அறியும் நீரோர் இல்லை) praises the envoy's knowledge, not his own birth, which Kural 681 (ஆன்ற குடிப்பிறத்தல்) names; that the host tests family by recital is read in from other verses. Illustration at best.

1967 (மாதவம் ஏற்கொண்டு மாயங்கள் பின்னை முயல்வார் பிறப்பும் அதுவே) and T1659 (பொய்த்தவஞ் செய்வார் புகுவர் நரகத்து) both condemn false austerity. The claimed difference of place is an accident of which verse is paired, and the Tirumanthiram's last lines are obscure; the gains clause about 'a Jain choice' is not supported.
1103 and 1106 are two moments of one rite. 1106 (இகழ்ந்தாள்) is flagged uncertain and need not mean shyness grown into reproach; 'one feeling across the rite' is sequence read as development.
links.text_issue: 1106 sense uncertain; speaker inferred from இகழ்ந்தாள்.

links.reason: 1471 (கண்கள் புடைத்து வீழ்ந்தார்) shows wives collapsing on the field; Naladiyar 25 turns wailing into a rebuke of household joy. The note itself says the epic makes no such turn, so teaches contradicts itself and both gains clauses are things lacking.

148 (காமர் காம பூமி) names a park of hills, falls, pools and deer, but no beloved or built features; M19 lines 102-105 list built wells, hills and pools. The note's 'with his beloved' and the later prison-news interruption are not in 148, and park scenes are conventional.
36 (நாக லோக நகுவதொத்து) and 50 (இந்திர உலகம் வந்திழிந்தது ஒக்கும்) are two ordinary praise comparisons; reading them as the two ends of a scale is the reader's, not stated in the verses.
links.text_issue: Verse 50 and 36 are both simple comparisons; 36 line 1 loose construction.

links.reason: 16 (பணித்து ஆங்கு விடுத்த) says only that a god taught him spells; 1289 does not name the mantra as that spell, and 16 does not identify the god with the dog (the marker admits this). The chain of gratitude is in other verses.

443 swears (காப்பேன் எனின் யான் அவனாக) to protect cows, renouncers, women and children; 1861 swears by his name (என் பெயர் சேறல் இன்றாய்) for the king's herd. The two cattle-raid vows are parallel, not development, and the friends' choice of a raid is not in 1861.

1378 (புலவிப் பொழுதும் கணவன் அகலின் உயிர் அகறல்) says a husband's going even in sulk takes the wife's life; it is Padumai's lament, not a sulk, so the risk Kural 1307 names (ஊடலின் உண்டாங்கோர் துன்பம் புணர்வது நீடுவதன்று கொல்) is stretched. The link needs a generous reading of the words.

2 of each book is an invocation of the Jina: Soolamani's light of the world (வினை போழ்ந்து... சுடராகி) and Cintamani's form brighter than flame. The note's distinction of act and form is thin, and Soolamani line 1 has a flagged misprint.

386 (நல் அறம் காக்க என்றாள்) and 405 (தவங்கள் தாயா, தந்தை நீ ஆகி) do pair the mother's leaving with new parentage, but 'aram had taken him up through the ascetic' is the note's gloss, not in either verse.

256's refrain (துக்கந் துக்கம்... சருவம் துக்கம்) is spoken by Neelakesi in mockery and refuted. Manimekalai 30 (துன்பம் தோற்றம் பற்றே காரணம்; இன்பம் வீடே பற்றிலி காரணம்) states the doctrine with its cause. The pair shows the caricature drops the cause. Type should read as a corrective, but the conflict is real.

109 (யூகியும் வஞ்சந் தன்னை... போகநன் னீரில் ஆட) and 110 (ஊரிற் தீ இடுவித்தானே) are neighbouring plot verses; the fire is Yugi's purpose, but verse 109 states the bathing as for another aim and says nothing of fire.
links.text_issue: Both flagged uncertain in line 3 of 109.

links.reason: 1616 (காதலன் முயங்குபு... சீற்றமொழி) shows an embrace and a plea that she give up anger; there is no crown at her feet. Kural 1304 (ஊடியவரை உணராமை வாடிய வள்ளி முதலரிந்தற்று) states the cost of not reconciling. The note's gains clause on the king's dignity is not in the Tamil.

770 (முதலொடும் கேடு வந்தால்... இருமுதல் கெடாமை கொள்வார்) is the kings' taunt about running to save capital; Kural 463 speaks of not undertaking deeds that lose capital for gain. 'Quoted by the side that loses' is not so, and what counts as capital is unfixed in 770.

2902 (துறக்கமும் வீடும் வேண்டேன்... பாதம் விரும்பி வழிபட்டு) is a devotion to a brother; T284 is devotion to God that grants release (பத்திமையாலே... முத்தி கொடுத்து). No shared claim is contradicted, and 'devotional bargain' is invented.

1144 (எதிர்நின்று கனற்றி என்னை... முகமன் சொல்லி) shows a warrior holding back and flattering, not a counsellor serving a quarrelsome king as in Kural 691 (அகலாது அணுகாது தீக்காய்வார் போல்க). The 'withheld admiration' in gains is not in the verse.

2177 (பன்றி எய்த வருமகன் ஆகும் என்று முரசு அறைவித்தான்) sets a condition and 2204 (பன்றியியற்றரும் பொறியும்... ஒருங்குடன் உதிர எய்தான்) meets it. This is a proclamation and its fulfilment, so the later unit answers the earlier.

27 (திரு நிற்ப... அரசு அஞ்சித் துறந்த) shows Civakan renouncing with every good intact and giving fear of kingship from hearing dharma, where Naladiyar 53 (நிலையாமை கண்டு... துறப்பர்) roots renunciation in seeing goods pass. The epic adds a case the quatrain does not foresee, and both gains are true.
1379 (கனக சித்திரன்... செப்பினான்) announces that Kanaka Chitran speaks and 1382 begins his speech; this is story order, and the teaching is only that a taunt follows.

1935 (உறுப்புறுப்பாக அரிந்தரிந்து ஊட்டி) gives a mirror punishment for those who killed deer for meat; Kural 255 ties flesh-eating to hell (அளறு), which one commentary reads as a mud pit. The verse's ground is killing and eating together, so 'meat itself, not cruelty' is overstated.

12 (நானிலம் கலந்து பொன் அரலும் நாடு) says the four regions are in one land; Porunaraatruppadai 218-225 exchanges each region's tunes and creatures in a mocking inversion of the karu. The epic lists, the poem swaps, so 'both let the regions share' and the other-side gains clause are not true.
1601 (இருந்தனர் இருவரும் இனிதின்) and 1602 (அரசியார் பொழில் அடைந்தாள்) are consecutive; the jester's fright is not in either verse, and the pair shows only story order.

1408 (நாஞ்சிலால் உழுது... புகழ் வித்தினான்) and 1415 (நாஞ்சிலால் உழுதிட்டான்) both turn the plough into a warrior's tool; 1415 does not name the hero, and the grand reading 'sign and tool of rule' is the note's. A shared image without much taught by the pairing.

1502 (இரங்கல் இன்றாய்... பரிவொடும் இருக்கும்) is Civakan's covert message through the bee and 1530 shows her holding her life; but 1530 says she lives from fear of harm to her husband (ஊனமும் பிரிவும் அஞ்சி), not by a rule of not grieving, and 1502's sense is uncertain. The link is real but the note misstates both ends.

1092 (அரவு சேர்ந்தென விழவுடை முதுநகர் விலாவிக் கின்றதே) is a real lament at his binding; 1683 (காவலன் காளை தன்னை சிறை செய்கின்றான் என்று) shows the crowd misreading the king. The paired scenes answer each other as plot, but 'a bride proves the fetter' is in 1684, not here.

Kural 1085 (கூற்றமோ கண்ணோ பிணையோ) and 1308 (சிலையோ வேற்கணோ மொழியோ மட நோக்கமோ... யாது நான் அறியேன்) share the list of 'is it this or that'; the epic then ends on காமமே, moving the cause from her to himself. The pairing teaches that turn and both gains are true.

1906 (இணை அடி பரவுவார்க் கெளியானை) and T1451 (திருவடி நீழல் சரண்) both say take refuge at one Lord's feet. But 1906 calls the Lord அருளாழியான் and ஊழி முதல், so the contrast of a Jina who gave up and a God of grace is not borne out, and T1451 names no god.

Manimekalai 29 lines 267-280 define a logical fallacy (இரண்டினும் சங்கயம் ஆய்), a technical doubt between proofs; Kural 353 (ஐயத்தின் நீங்கித் தெளிந்தார்க்கு) is about a mind freed from doubt. The link rests on the word 'doubt'.
192 (கனவு... மிக்கோர் சொல்வார்) and 63 (அவள் கனவு உரைப்பக் கேட்டு) both show a dream read as forecast; the note adds only the contrast of what each reader names. A recurring motif and little more.
